newsitem.title: USA: Sears September same-store sales up 7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sears September same-store sales up 7 pct.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said Thursday its same-store domestic revenues for the five weeks ended October 5 increased seven percent over the comparable period a year ago.
Total domestic store revenues for the five weeks rose 10.3 percent, to $2.47 billion from $2.24 billion for the five weeks ended October 7, 1995, the retailer said.

"September gains for both softlines and hardlines reflected strong demand for back-to-school clothing, work and leisure apparel and home improvement products, as customers responded to our wider assortments, quality brands and emphasis on value," said Arthur Martinez, Sears chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement.

"Women's ready to wear, children's and men's apparel experienced substantial growth, as did accessories and shoes. In hardlines, lawn and garden products sold exceptionally well, along with Craftsman tools and hardware," he said.
"Customers also heavily shopped Sears off-the-mall locations, resulting in double-digit comparable store increases for Sears hardware, HomeLife furniture and Sears dealer stores," he said.
For the five weeks ended October 5, Sears reported total revenues of $3.42 billion, nine percent above the $3.14 billion in the same period of 1995.
For the 35 weeks ended October 5, Sears reported total revenues of $23.63 billion, 8.9 percent above the $21.70 billion in the same period of 1995.
Sears owns and operates about 2,300 department and specialty stores in the United States.
